title: Your Skin Is Still Healing After It Looks Healed
caps: Your skin is still healing after it looks healed.
When a small gap in your skin closes,
it looks finished in a week or two,
but it isn't.
Underneath, the work has already begun.
First,
your body seals it and calls in its cleaning crews.
New cells creep in from the edges,
and repair cells lay down fresh collagen.
Quickly, a little messily, like scaffolding.
But for months,
sometimes a year or more,
the skin keeps quietly rebuilding.
Then,
quick collagen is traded for stronger fibers drawn slowly into line.
The spot grows flatter and softer, paler.
Even then,
rebuilt skin usually ends up at most around 80% as strong as before.
So the skin you think of as healed is still being gently rewoven,
long after you've forgotten it.
If you're feeling a little calmer,
tap like and follow.
